correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, dehomogenization at central-weight subsets contains all n signed basis monomials and only their nonnegative combinations, giving A^n. At an extreme singleton, all generators factor into a_i=t_i/t_1 and b_i=t_i; their algebra is the standard prime 2-by-(n-1) rank-one determinantal algebra, as proved by its Segre parametrization. Complementation provides the same result at co-singletons. Each rank-one cone is normal, smooth outside the origin, and singular at its origin; the complete standard-affine cover therefore proves exactly 2n isolated singular points. The projective Segre cone has vertex integral class group Z via Pic(P1 x P^(n-2))/Z(1,1), confirmed by primitive rays containing a unimodular basis. Its canonical class is (-2,-(n-1)) modulo (1,1), zero or torsion precisely if n=3; Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity equals deg(P1 x P^(n-2))=n-1. The exponent polytope is the unit n-cube minus two unimodular corner simplices, so normalized volume n!-2. Finite checker replays exact membership checks for n=3..7; it supplements, not substitutes for, general proofs. Residual dependence is on standard primary determinantal normality, primeness, and toric class-group theorems.

originality.rationale: Definition 4.1, Remark 4.2 and Proposition 4.7 of Michałek–Oeding–Zwiernik (arXiv:1212.1515) already cover this T_(1,n-1) construction and its full homogeneous quadratic relations, and Example 4.4 covers the n=3 octahedron. Their detailed Section 5 local-singularity results concern T_(2,n), a different family. The known six-nodal toric intersection of two quadrics additionally covers the n=3 special case (Cheltsov et al., Proposition 6.1). Neither inspected article establishes the present higher-n *pointwise* rank-one chart isomorphisms, integral local divisor groups, exact singular count, or Q-Gorenstein boundary. Related indexed multiview Segre-cone findings are mathematically separate varieties. An equivalent unindexed historical result remains possible; negative search alone was not used as novelty proof.

value.rationale: This naturally defined binary Segre projection is established in secant-cumulant toric geometry, with an intrinsic nontrivial change in canonical singularity type as n varies. The result determines *all* affine chart rings and pointwise integral local divisor class groups, exact Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities and the Q-Gorenstein locus throughout an infinite projective toric family, rather than a random numerical slice or a cosmetic restatement of its already-known toric quadratic equations. The dimension-three base case is old; the higher-dimensional boundary and complete local singularity geometry are structurally motivated and needed for birational classification.
